examples.label: cap_dac_override on vim -> blank root's password in /etc/passwd
OSCP Ch17 — recursive getcap scan from root (spot cap_setuid binaries)
OSCP Ch17 — perl cap_setuid exploit: setuid(0) then spawn shell (GTFOBins)

notes: Cap flags: +ep effective+permitted, +ei effective+inheritable, +p permitted, = clear. High-value: cap_setuid, cap_setgid, cap_sys_admin, cap_dac_override. OSCP Ch17: getcap -r / (recursive from root) is the standard scan. cap_setuid+ep on perl/python means any user can setuid(0). GTFOBins confirms the one-liner. Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 17 (Linux Privilege Escalation).

recommended.note: Which capabilities are abusable and how.
SUID enumeration is the sibling technique.

name: Capabilities - Enumerate and Abuse
description: File capabilities grant slices of root power without SUID. Enumerate them, then abuse high-value ones - e.g. a binary with cap_dac_override can overwrite /etc/passwd to blank root's password.

defense.why_it_works: Linux capabilities subdivide root privileges into distinct units. If a binary has a dangerous capability set (cap_dac_override, cap_setuid, cap_sys_admin), it can perform privileged operations without being SUID. cap_dac_override bypasses all file permission checks -- so a vim binary with this capability can edit /etc/passwd to remove root's password hash.
defense.prerequisites: A binary with a dangerous capability set (cap_dac_override, cap_setuid, cap_net_raw) accessible to the attacker. getcap tool to enumerate.
defense.impact: Privilege escalation via a seemingly normal binary. cap_dac_override allows writing to /etc/passwd. cap_setuid allows setting UID to 0. cap_sys_admin is near-equivalent to full root.
defense.detection: getcap executed to enumerate capabilities. vim or other editor used to modify /etc/passwd. Auditd: write to /etc/passwd by vim process (non-root). EDR: setuid(0) call from non-root process via capability.
defense.artifacts: Auditd: write to /etc/passwd by vim (non-root) | /etc/passwd modification event | File integrity alert on /etc/passwd
defense.prevention: Audit all capabilities: find /usr/bin /usr/sbin -type f -exec getcap {} +. Remove unnecessary capabilities. Only grant specific required capabilities (e.g., cap_net_raw for ping, not cap_dac_override for editors). Monitor /etc/passwd with file integrity monitoring.
defense.misconfiguration: vim or other editor granted cap_dac_override capability without operational necessity, allowing any user to read/write any file on the system including /etc/passwd.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Dangerous capability set
/usr/bin/vim.basic = cap_dac_override+eip

# This allows:
echo -e ':%s/^root:[^:]*:/root::/\nwq!' | /usr/bin/vim.basic -es /etc/passwd
# Removes root password hash -> su gives root
defense.secure_config:
# Audit and remove unnecessary capabilities
cap_set=$(find /usr/bin /usr/sbin -exec getcap {} + 2>/dev/null)
echo "$cap_set"  # review all entries

# Remove capability from vim
setcap -r /usr/bin/vim.basic

# Only grant minimal required capabilities:
# ping: cap_net_raw (not cap_dac_override)
setcap cap_net_raw+ep /usr/bin/ping
